2. **Hunk marks reconcile by canonical, versioned fingerprints.** [Fingerprint code](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jj-diff/src/review_fingerprint.rs#L10) (S00028/S00060:10–54,92–153; S00063:176–195,259–288) uses exact whitespace, uncollapsed/unhighlighted changed lines, side, source text, EOF-newline state and up to three unchanged context lines on each side. It excludes absolute line/group position, keeps CRLF significant, and maps display groups to canonical groups when whitespace is hidden. [Mark reconciliation](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-review/src/file_state.rs#L116) (S00024/S00034:74–134,194–235) has an identity/version fast path, otherwise inherits only fingerprints unique in both old and new snapshots. Ambiguous/new groups become `ChangedSinceReview`; removed reviewed groups remain counted. Legacy file/hunk marks and missing/version-mismatched snapshots follow more conservative rules. Thus matching hunk state can survive some edits or rebases; universal mark survival is not supported.

3. **Notes use a different, more conservative matcher.** [Note reconciliation](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-review/src/reconcile.rs#L44) (S00010:44–69) checks resolved status first; absent path in the current *diff* yields `Orphaned`; changed full file-pair identity yields `Stale`; only then can matching side/line/excerpt yield `Current`. A still-existing file can be orphaned because it left the diff. Stored `anchor_context` is not consulted by this function. Hunk fingerprint migration is not note migration. “Survives a rebase” therefore needs separate evidence for marks and notes.

4. **Content identity does not establish provenance isolation.** [Identity computation](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/diff/entry.rs#L43) (S00108/S00115:43–74) hashes both native tree sides, including blob/executable, symlink/tree/submodule/absence and projection identity; it does not hash repository or immutable commit identity. Rebase invariance requires those inputs to remain equal. Store keys are literally `change_id|path` (S00029/S00041:62–64); the note schema has change/path/file identity and anchor data, but no repository, immutable commit or operation ID (S00025/S00039:15–47). The ordinary report filters via the resolved change ID, but the [owned-vector entrypoint](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/review_notes.rs#L55) passes supplied notes unchanged to reconciliation (S00026/S00037:35–71). A caller can supply another change's notes; content-identical divergent versions or copied changes can share the tested identities. This is a source-level missing provenance check, not an executed demonstration of wrong-note migration. The handoff's “must not silently migrate” is a desired guarantee, not an upstream guarantee.

5. **Filesystem persistence is independent of reconciliation and native history.** [Persistence code](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-review/src/store/persistence/filesystem.rs#L46) (S00027/S00035:46–155) stores `review_store.json` in app config, optionally overridden by `JAYJAY_REVIEW_STORE_PATH`. Refresh compares mtime/length; save writes a unique sibling temp file and renames it. These functions contain no lock/CAS spanning refresh–mutate–save. Two readers of the same state can each publish a complete file and lose the other's update. Read failure returns empty state; malformed JSON preservation is attempted but rename failure is ignored; save errors are logged. Atomic rename prevents partial-file visibility, not lost updates or proven crash durability. A native JJ source backup would not automatically include this app-level file. The retained child persistence warning is supported, with runtime behavior still untested here.

### Reviewable proposal — shared computation with PM-owned provenance and persistence

**Decision requested for future planning, not presumed granted:** approve a bounded compatibility evaluation of the pinned pure primitives/diff/review computations, and separately decide whether persistent file/hunk review marks should inherit across verified JJ successors. The recommended candidate is a pure Rust service behind Source Control using PM's canonical storage; retain the existing implementation as the comparison option. Adopting all of JayJay core or either shell is not necessary to obtain this benefit.

**Benefit.** One computation path can keep Slint diffs, file review and agent/Chat summaries consistent, while preserving matching reviewed hunks after local rewrites and visibly retaining stale/orphaned notes. The existing compare identity and routing owners stay authoritative.

**Concrete proposed behavior and choices.**

- Capture an owner-issued review snapshot with PM `repo_id`, backend/workspace/source identity, exact left/right immutable revision references and originating operation, file-pair native identity, side/anchor and render/fingerprint version. A content hash helps match content; it never proves repository or revision ownership. Validate caller-supplied note collections against that snapshot before computation.
- Keep original note/mark provenance immutable. A successor reconciliation is a new result referencing both snapshots; cross-repository, wrong-change and divergent-commit matches cannot silently become current. Recommended policy: only explicit, owner-verified successor lineage can carry state forward. Alternative: intentionally share change-level review across branches/versions, with visible source provenance and an explicit sharing choice. The latter is more convenient but can overstate what was actually reviewed.
- If hunk inheritance is accepted, use unique canonical fingerprint matches and conservative ambiguity/version handling as an evaluated candidate. Do not automatically apply this algorithm to existing document/bundle annotations. Notes may remain stale even when one hunk's mark survives; explain those states separately and preserve an explicit reanchor/review action.

### Primary evidence and corrections to older architecture prose

**Native stores and indirection.** At jj 0.45.1 (S00114/S00123:14–17), [repo initialization](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/repo.rs#L219) (S00072/S00158:219–261) creates separately selected commit, operation, op-head, index and submodule stores. [Workspace loading](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/workspace.rs#L568) (S00069/S00084/S00088:369–407,568–630) resolves a secondary `.jj/repo` path file relative to `.jj`; local `.jj/working_copy` remains separate. Creation prefers a relative path where possible. The native code is stronger evidence than the handoff's Kaizen patch, whose merge/release status is not needed to establish this behavior.

[GitBackend init/load](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/git_backend.rs#L228) (S00068/S00086:228–362) has internal, colocated and external backing stores. Internal Git is `store/git`; the persisted `git_target` is resolved from the JJ store directory; `store/extra` loads independently. A secondary workspace copy alone, or a backing Git copy alone, omits required native state. Relative Windows targets are normalized for WSL, while the code explicitly says absolute targets are not simultaneously portable inside/outside WSL (311–325). [Path canonicalization](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/git_backend.rs#L605) (S00089:605–617) deliberately preserves the final `.git` component because fully following it can change a colocated repository into a bare interpretation. Relocation is a semantic mapping, not blind path normalization.

**Git dependencies are real, including alternates.** The [Git repository-layout manual](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitrepository-layout) (S00111/S00121:211–236,258–267; S00150:405–427) describes gitfiles, object alternates, common-dir, shallow metadata, submodules and linked-worktree administrative data. Relative alternate paths are based at the object database, relative `commondir` at the Git directory; these differ from JJ's `.jj/repo` and `git_target` bases. A negative literal search in jj is not evidence that alternates are unsupported. JJ's manifest declares gix 0.87.1 (S00123:63–70); that release tag resolves to Gitoxide commit `3ebca8b66017ab2dd02a38f75f78f485bee1ded8` (S00131/S00132). [Object loading](https://github.com/GitoxideLabs/gitoxide/blob/3ebca8b66017ab2dd02a38f75f78f485bee1ded8/gix-odb/src/store_impls/dynamic/load_index.rs#L233) (S00112/S00118:233–268) uses recursively resolved alternates for loose and packed objects. [The resolver](https://github.com/GitoxideLabs/gitoxide/blob/3ebca8b66017ab2dd02a38f75f78f485bee1ded8/gix-odb/src/alternate/mod.rs#L41) (S00113/S00117:41–82) detects cycles/deduplicates paths but joins parsed paths to its initial `objects_directory`. Exact nested-relative behavior and environment-alternate parity need isolated cases before a custom closure walker is certified. The release/source match is inspected; no dependency build or runtime equivalence is asserted.

**Operation history reaches beyond current bookmarks.** [View and Operation structures](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/op_store.rs#L248) (S00070/S00087/S00090:248–261,358–380) record view heads/bookmarks/remote state/desired workspace commits and operation parents plus transitive rewrite predecessor mappings. [Operation commit references](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/operation.rs#L141) (S00073/S00099:141–153) include predecessor commits for rebuilding the index. [Default index construction](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/default_index/store.rs#L241) (S00074/S00093:241–345) walks retained operation ancestry, operation/view commit references and commit parents. Missing/corrupt default indexes can be rebuilt (S00096:519–554), but only if the required underlying closure exists. This does not prove every custom index/backend is safely discardable.

The older [architecture document](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/docs/technical/architecture.md#L9) (S00081/S00094:11–18,29–43,78–88) is incomplete even at the supplied pin. JayJay's actual core manifest contradicts “jj-lib only used by CLI”; `WorkingCopy` is now a trait (S00160:51–75). Newer native metadata can be read from Git change-id/conflict headers, while extras can override the change ID and contain older conflict trees/predecessors (GitBackend S00125:691–715; S00128:835–865). Native extras/operation history therefore cannot be dropped merely because some metadata is in Git headers. The writer handles a Git-ID/different-extras collision by holding the extras-table lock and adjusting the committer timestamp until unique (S00130:1400–1474), rather than categorically erroring as older prose suggests; its comment still admits a distributed rsync race. These corrections preserve, rather than invalidate, the multi-store lead.

**GC protection is not a backup fence.** `refs/jj/keep/*` are Git GC roots, not the operation log. GitBackend recreates them from index heads plus qualifying newer refs, then GCs extras and invokes Git GC (S00126:902–987; S00127:1558–1590). The timestamp logic documents re-import races. [Operation-store GC](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/simple_op_store.rs#L277) (S00083/S00129:277–316) follows selected heads/ancestors/views with age protection and notes a timestamp check/use race. `jj util gc` defaults to two weeks, accepts `--expire now`, and runs operation GC before backend GC (S00080/S00106:26–67). A backup must retain the intended roots/object closure through capture; ordinary native GC mitigations are not evidence of JJI-008's all-store fence.

**Workspace view, physical registry and actual files are different observations.** The operation view says what *should* be checked out; local working-copy state says the last completed update (S00087:258–261). The physical [workspace registry](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/workspace_store.rs#L104) (S00071/S00091:104–128,167–192) is a separate `workspace_store/index`, storing names/paths relative to repo where possible under its own lock. The [local proto](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/protos/local_working_copy.proto#L19) (S00076/S00085:19–78) records file types/stats/conflict-materialization state, tree terms/labels, sparse prefixes, Watchman state, checkout operation and workspace name. Actual unsnapshotted bytes are separate. [Working-copy documentation](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/docs/working-copy.md) (S00157:9–29,69–118) explains automatic tracking/snapshotting, ignored files, shared and stale workspaces. Native freshness distinguishes updated/stale/sibling operations and can treat differing operation IDs as fresh when trees match (S00079/S00104:348–399). Do not equate all operation-ID differences with dirty/stale files. The default submodule store is a stub containing a path/name (S00162:22–51), not proof child source objects are present.

**Capture ordering must be demonstrated.** [Transaction publication](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/transaction.rs#L125) (S00075/S00092:125–172,202–240) writes view, operation and index before publishing heads; unpublished operations can exist outside the visible head set. One local workspace mutation lock reloads its state, then finish writes tree and checkout state separately (S00077/S00098:2662–2690; S00101:2940–2965). It does not freeze arbitrary editor writes, all workspaces, every external object store or GC. Equal op heads before/after capture do not prove an unchanged physical file image.

Nor is acquiring a `ReadonlyRepo` automatically a nonmutating discovery step: `load_at_head` may reconcile divergent heads (S00072/S00095:714–736), index loading may rebuild files (S00096), and workspace-store loading can initialize missing storage (S00091:116–125). Exact-operation loading avoids head reconciliation but does not by itself avoid all cache writes. Preserve original evidence; run reconstruction/repair only in the isolated copy under the accepted owner protocol.
